candidates.source_summary: Rochdale will receive a new Young Futures Hub, bringing together support and opportunities for young people in the local community
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale will receive a new Young Futures Hub, bringing together support and opportunities for young people in the local community. The new hub will bring together mental health support, employment and skills opportunities, sport, creative activities and crime prevention services. Rochdale Council will also receive support through the Local Youth Transformation programme to strengthen leadership, train its workforce and build lasting local partnerships. The new Young Futures Hub will provide young people in Rochdale aged 10 to 18 — and up to 25 for those with SEND — with access to seamless, holistic support. Alongside open-access sport, creative activities and trusted youth workers, the hub will connect young people with mental health support, skills and training, routes into employment and crime prevention services. The expansion forms part of the Government’s National Youth Strategy, Youth Matters, launched by Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy in December, 2025, and co-produced with 14,000 young people through the State of the Nation survey. The survey highlighted that many young people have been left without access to safe, supportive environments or a community to belong to, while reliance on online interaction has grown in the absence of face-to-face opportunities. candidates.source_summary: Parking restrictions and traffic calming have been given the green light to make a "dangerous road" in Middleton safer.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Parking restrictions and traffic calming have been given the green light to make a “dangerous road” in Middleton safer. Last night, Middleton Township Committee approved a traffic order which will introduce three pedestrian crossing islands, extend bus stops, reduce on-street parking and narrow parts of Grimshaw Lane following problems with speeding, serious crashes, including a fatality, and inconsiderate parking blocking buses. The scheme was called in to be considered by the committee following objections from 11 residents, with the main concern being the loss of parking outside homes. After the meeting, Cllr Dylan Williams, ward councillor and Rochdale Council portfolio holder for highways and facilities, shared: “It has taken four-and-a-half years to get to this point. The road is very dangerous. There have been multiple RTAs, parked cars crashed into, property damaged repeatedly and a fatality. “The road layout was identified as a major factor in the number of accidents and this scheme addresses this. “The islands narrow the road and force the cars to slow down. The narrowing of junctions with disabled access crossings include Shawbury Street, Sedgley Street and the two Sandy Lanes. “We carried out extensive consultation on this scheme. Apart from the 11 objectors, everyone we spoke to was very supportive. “The meeting became very heated with some of the objectors who attended. The main point of contention was parking.

candidates.source_title: Hat trick of announcements as Middleton’s regeneration moves up a gear – Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.source_summary: A hat trick of announcements has cemented Middleton’s renewed regeneration drive, as its Mayoral Development Corporation continues to take shape.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A hat trick of announcements has cemented Middleton’s renewed regeneration drive, as its Mayoral Development Corporation continues to take shape. Among them is news that the Middleton Old Grammar School, recently bought by the council, is expected to announce a new tenant before the end of the year. Founded in 1582, the building in Boarshaw Road aimed to provide free education to children in the parish of Middleton. More recently, it was used as a wedding and events venue before the council took the opportunity to buy the heritage asset when it went up for sale. A feasibility study is now on going, with a view to the building being repaired, refurbished and reopened for community use in the future. The news was announced at an event at Middleton Arena to update residents and businesses about the results of an engagement exercise titled, ‘Our Town, Our Future’ and on going work to create a Mayoral Development Corporation to further drive regeneration in the town. Chaired by the proposed chairs of Middleton’s MDC, Steve Coogan and Rose Marley, and attended by Mayor of Greater Manchester, Bev Craig, and Rochdale Borough Council leader, Councillor Neil Emmott, the event attracted more than 500 residents and local business leaders. The announcements followed news that the council is in the process of acquiring long derelict Warwick Mill and neighbouring 1960s office block, London House, with a view to bringing the mill back into use, possibly as new homes, and demolishing London House. In a further boost, attendees also learned that the Middleton Scout Hut will be repurposed as a community venue, with a full programme of activities and training opportunities for young people. The council owned venue on Long Street has been vacant for 13 years and the council has now agreed a long-term lease with charitable organisation, the Groundwork Trust. Proposals for the building include the creation of a hub for workshops to teach ecology and construction skills. The building will also serve as a base for local environmental projects, and, while opportunities for young people will be a key focus, it will also be a space for community groups to get together to help tackle social isolation.

candidates.source_title: Council urges families to apply on time for secondary school places – Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.source_summary: 331 families submitted their applications late last year.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Parents are being urged not to miss the deadline to apply for their child’s secondary school place after 331 families submitted their applications late last year. This warning has been triggered after only half of last year’s late applicants (51%) were offered a place at their first-choice school, compared with 87% of those who applied on time. While there is no guarantee that any applicant will be offered a place at their preferred secondary school and a number of other factors are taken into account, completing an application on time is an important part of the admissions process. This is because late applications are not processed until after National Offer Day (1 March 2027), the day when families discover which school their child will attend. Schools do not reserve places for late applications either, meaning they may already be full before a late application is considered. Councillor Rachel Massey, cabinet member for children’s services and education, said: "Choosing the right secondary school for a child is one of the most important decisions families make and it's not something to be left until the last minute. “As a parent who has gone through the process already, I know myself how much thought goes into making these preferences as ultimately this is the school that will shape your child’s educational journey and where they will sit their GCSEs. “There is time left to decide which school is best for your child and to help you, there are upcoming open evenings at local schools to inform your decision. Don’t leave it too late as it is important you find the right place for your child's future.”

candidates.source_title: Wildlife mural created in Middleton as part of Kenya arts exchange
candidates.source_summary: Artists from Rochdale and Kenya have created a 15-metre-high wildlife mural on Brook House in Middleton town centre.
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The artwork on Oldham Road is part of an international exchange project focusing on endangered species and ecosystems.

The mural has been created through the Endangered Exchange project by Rochdale artist AYLO, also known as Hayley Garner, and Victoria Firth, founder of The Wild Mural Project.

They have been working with local artist Jamie Buckley and Kenyan artist Ninah Tanya as part of the project.

The artwork measures around 15 metres high and 10 metres wide.

It features a hen harrier, large heath butterfly, emperor dragonfly, sphagnum moss and wildfires.

The words "Save our tomorrow today" also appear in Swahili, while the design includes Kanga fabric associated with Kenyan culture.

The project has been developed in partnership with Lancashire Wildlife Trust.

Hayley Garner said: "Victoria and I came up with the idea of 'Endangered Exchange' - an international collaboration that could create vibrant community driven art that inspires a deeper connection between people and the planet.

"It's not just painting, it's about developing artists and giving opportunities they might never otherwise have had, connecting communities across the world and showing how creativity can bring people together."

Ninah Tanya travelled from Nairobi to Middleton for a two-week artist residency after spending the past year being mentored by Victoria Firth in Kenya.

She said: "This is the biggest mural I've worked on and it has been an amazing experience. I've visited Rochdale too to see the murals there, painted by artists I admire, and the town hall is beautiful."

Jamie Buckley is due to travel to Kenya next month for the second part of the exchange.

He will work with the other artists and local communities on workshops, wildlife research and a second mural focusing on Kenya's natural environment.

Victoria Firth said: "We only have one planet to live on, so we need to take care of it. I think this new Middleton mural shares a powerful message about our climate, and species that will disappear, as well as creating a connection between Middleton and Kenya."

Councillor Sue Smith, cabinet member for communities and co-operation at Rochdale Borough Council, said the project followed feedback from residents through the Middleton Co-operating "Our Town, Our Future" engagement.

She said: "This striking new mural is a powerful reminder that climate change is one of the greatest challenges facing our planet and the wildlife that depends on it."

The project is being recorded for a documentary covering the artists' journeys, mentoring and cultural exchange.

The UK stage forms part of the Rochdale Creates cultural programme and is part-funded by The Butterfly Effected CIC, Rochdale Development Agency and Rochdale Borough Council.

The Kenyan stage is being supported by The Wild Mural Projects, Caparol Paints Kenya and Turtle Bay Beach Club in Watamu.

Littleborough Brass Band, conducted by Max Stannard, performed Snow Island by Thierry Deleruyelle ahead of competing in the Third Section at the finals.

Wardle Community Band, conducted by Jane Conway, performed Heroes of the North by Peter Graham before taking part in the Fourth Section contest.

Brass band adjudicator and conductor Matthew Ryan also attended the concert and gave both bands feedback on their performances.

Littleborough Brass Band secretary Jonathan Coomer said: “It’s important preparation for the bands to perform their respective pieces outside the band room and in front of an audience.

“Matthew provided each band with valuable feedback and insight as both bands continue to prepare this week ahead of the final on Sunday.”

The concert was attended by a packed audience at St Andrew’s Church.

Both bands will compete at the National Brass Band Championships of Great Britain at York Barbican on 20 September.

candidates.source_title: Wedding venue plan refused over ‘harm’ development could cause - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Plans to turn a former Conservative club and bowling green into a modern wedding and events venue have been refused after the benefits of the scheme were outweighed by the harm it could cause
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to turn a former Conservative club and bowling green into a modern wedding and events venue have been refused after the benefits of the scheme were outweighed by the harm it could cause. Mr M Suleman appealed to the Planning Inspectorate about the length of time Rochdale Council took to consider his application to turn the former Middleton Conservative Club and Kohinoor Banqueting Hall into a new multi-functional events space in Long Street. Plans submitted in February included a part single/part two-storey side extension, external stairway and retaining wall, creation of access to rear and conversion of a former bowling green into a parking area. The appeal was launched while the council considered issues including pedestrian access and safe routes to the proposed wedding venue; the impact of noise on nearby residents, including the first-floor flat within the building which may be used by a caretaker; air quality; and concerns about protected species that might be affected by the development. Planning inspector Roger Catchpole said: “The council failed to give notice within the statutory time period but has set out its putative reasons for refusal. “I find the main issues to be the effect of the proposal on the character and appearance of the area, bearing in mind the special attention that should be paid to the desirability of preserving the special interest of the adjacent Grade II* listed building, known as Long Street Methodist Church, Long Street Methodist Sunday School and the extent to which it would preserve or enhance the character or appearance of the Middleton Town Centre Conservation Area.” Mr Catchpole agreed with the council that the plans, including the extension, were “generally appropriate in terms of the established street scene” and that it was set back from important historic elements of Long Street. “However, I cannot rule out direct harm to the fabric of the listed building given the proximity of the ramp and the lack of detail concerning its construction,” he said.

candidates.source_title: International exchange: Middleton goes wild for nature inspired mural – Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.source_summary: Artists from Rochdale and Kenya have brought a huge new endangered wildlife themed mural to Brook House in Middleton.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Drivers and pedestrians in Middleton town centre are noticing some new wildlife popping up along their commute. Artists from Rochdale and Samburu, Kenya have brought a huge new endangered wildlife themed mural to Brook House on Oldham Road, encouraging residents to understand the importance of ecosystems as well as the conservation efforts that enhance wildlife and protect the planet. Lead artists - AYLO (Hayley Garner) from Rochdale and Kenyan based Victoria Firth, founder of global arts initiative The Wild Mural Project have been mentoring local artist Jamie Buckley and Kenyan based Ninah Tanya, to create their first international masterpiece in Middleton. Hayley, curator of the Common Walls International Mural Festival that has transformed public spaces with large-scale artwork in Rochdale said: "Victoria and I came up with the idea of 'Endangered Exchange' - an international collaboration that could create vibrant community driven art that inspires a deeper connection between people and the planet. It's not just painting, it's about developing artists and giving opportunities they might never otherwise have had, connecting communities across the world and showing how creativity can bring people together." A large heath butterfly - classed as endangered in the UK features in the artwork. Developed in partnership with the Lancashire Wildlife Trust, the Endangered Exchange initiative follows 'The Herds', the groundbreaking public art project that visited Heywood last year as part of Manchester International Festival and Rochdale's year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture, encouraging communities to renew their bond with the natural world. The striking 15 metre high x 10 metre wide mural features species that tell an interconnected story: a Hen Harrier, large heath butterfly - classed as endangered in the UK, emperor dragon fly, sphagnum moss that holds water and allows peat to form, and wildfires. Referencing the projects connection to Keyna, the phrase 'Save our tomorrow today' is written in Swahili - a call to notice what is around us, understand how connected it all is and to protect these landscapes before the warning becomes a loss we cannot reverse. The new mural has been designed to represent mounting pressure being placed on landscapes that may appear strong but are held together by delicate relationships between water, plants, insects, birds and climate. The artwork also features Kanga, a striking fabric that reflects the rich culture of Keyna.

candidates.source_title: East Lancashire Railway to introduce BSL interpreter on Santa Specials
candidates.source_summary: The East Lancashire Railway will provide a British Sign Language interpreter on selected Santa Special trains for the first time this year.
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The service will be available on selected journeys between Rawtenstall and Bury from 29 November.

The interpreter service is being funded through a partnership with Chorley-based foster care and special needs provider Family Care.

Families will be able to book places from November, with limited spaces available.

The railway introduced its first SEND Santa Special in 2023 for children with special educational needs.

Changes included reducing flashing lights on the station footbridge, spacing out characters, extending the arrival window and providing quiet carriages.

Passengers were also given signs to indicate whether they wanted characters to limit their interaction or be more enthusiastic.

The SEND service has since been expanded to several trains and dates.

British Sign Language interpreter Marie Marshall will work on selected Santa Specials this year.

She said: "I am really looking forward to being part of the Santa Express team so deaf children can have the same experience as other children."

Phil Williamson, director at Family Care Group, said: "We're proud to be supporting the ELR with their dedicated SEND Santa Specials which provide a safe, welcoming and inclusive environment for families to enjoy this amazing trip.

"As a family-owned and community focused organisation, we have a real passion for providing opportunities for all children in the Lancashire and North West, particularly those with special educational needs and disabilities. Our new partnership with East Lancashire Railway reflects our own strong commitment to supporting SEND children in the work we do."

East Lancashire Railway chairman Mike Kelly said: "We are incredibly proud to have been the first heritage railway to introduce dedicated SEND Santa Specials in 2023, creating a safe, welcoming and inclusive environment where families could experience the magic of Christmas together.

"Since then, we have expanded the programme each year, ensuring even more children and families can enjoy this special experience. In 2026, we are delighted to extend our reach further by providing the support of a professional British Sign Language (BSL) signer, making our events even more accessible.

"As we look ahead to the 40th anniversary of our Santa Specials in 2027, our vision is simple: that every visitor, whatever their additional needs or challenges, can experience the wonder and excitement of Christmas and create treasured memories that will last a lifetime."

The Santa Specials will run from late November until Christmas Eve.

More information is available at www.eastlancsrailway.org.uk.

candidates.source_title: Thousands set for Bury BID 10K as running festival returns
candidates.source_summary: Thousands of runners are expected to take part in the Bury Running Festival when it returns on Sunday 20 September.
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The festival includes the Bury BID 10K and Mini and Junior races for younger runners.

The event is organised by Jane Tomlinson's Run For All in partnership with Bury Council and title sponsor Bury BID.

The 10K will start and finish outside The Rock Shopping Centre, with the route taking runners through Tottington and along Bury Road before joining the Kirklees Trail and returning towards Bury town centre.

Children aged three to eight can take part in the 1.5K Mini event with a parent or guardian, while runners aged nine to 14 can enter the 2.5K Junior race.

Bury BID is supporting the event as title sponsor for the third consecutive year.

Participants can also raise money for charities, with Backup, Bury Football Club, Jigsaw and the Jane Tomlinson Appeal named as official charity partners.

Tristan Batley-Kyle, operations director at Run For All, said: "We're looking forward to welcoming thousands of runners and supporters to Bury for what promises to be another fantastic day of running and community spirit.

"Whether you're taking on the 10K, cheering from the sidelines or supporting one of our Mini and Junior runners, there's a real sense of occasion on race day. We'd like to wish everyone the very best of luck and thank all of our partners, volunteers and supporters for helping make the event possible."

Councillor Tamoor Tariq, cabinet member for Adult Care, Health and Public Service Reform at Bury Council, said: "The Bury Running Festival has become a fantastic fixture in our events calendar, bringing together people of all ages and abilities to get active, support good causes and celebrate our borough's strong community spirit. The Bury BID 10K and Mini and Junior races showcase the very best of Bury, encouraging healthier lifestyles while also attracting visitors and supporting our local businesses.

"I'll be joining the runners again this year and, while I certainly won't be troubling the leaders at the front of the race, I'm looking forward to taking part alongside everyone else and doing my best to make it to the finish line. One of the things I love most about this event is that it welcomes people of all abilities, whether you're chasing a personal best, taking part for a charity close to your heart, or simply determined to complete the course.

"We'd encourage everyone to come along, whether you're running, volunteering or cheering participants on from the sidelines. It's always a fantastic day for Bury and a wonderful celebration of community spirit."

candidates.source_title: Man crashed into Rochdale pub after police chase inquest hears
candidates.source_summary: Will Place had been celebrating England's Euro 2024 win in Rochdale hours before the fatal crash.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man died after he drove at speeds of up to 70mph during a police chase which ended when he lost control and crashed into a pub, an inquest heard. Will Place, 23, had been drinking in Rochdale, Greater Manchester, while watching the England vs Slovakia match at Euro 2024. He got behind the wheel of his car at 03:00 BST the next day. Shortly after, police in a marked van saw him pass a red light on Manchester Road and officers began a pursuit of the car when it failed to stop. Rochdale Coroner's Court was shown CCTV footage of Place driving at speeds of up to 70mph through residential streets before police called off the chase. The jury heard he carried on driving before ploughing into a pub. The Assistant Coroner Lisa Judge told the court that Place lost control of his car and crashed at high speed into the White Lion pub in Heywood on 1 July 2024. Police arrived 70 seconds later but the car had already caught fire and the building partially collapsed. Place was pronounced dead at just after 04:00. A post-mortem examination later found he had suffered catastrophic injuries and he was twice the legal limit for drink-driving.
